name: Hillel
title: Temple Court Scribe
description: A court scribe tasked with recording the formal questioning of Jesus in the Temple courts and the routine business of the livestock markets ahead of Passover. His dual records reveal a striking parallel between the inspection of Passover lambs and the public examination of Jesus.

attitude.neutral: Professional, precise, and focused on documenting what actually happened.
attitude.positive: Becomes animated when pointing out the pattern between the lamb records and Jesus's trial.
attitude.negative: Cautious about drawing conclusions that might be seen as heretical by his superiors.

background: Hillel's role gives him a unique vantage point on both the Temple's commercial operations and the religious authorities' attempts to trap Jesus. His records of the Passover lamb selection and inspection schedule provide the key to understanding the typological pattern the investigator is uncovering.
